app.logs.apps-load-failed: Failed to read the app list:
app.logs.detail-empty: Click any row on the left to see its details
app.logs.sensitive-note: Contains what the app submitted: host password, sudo password, private key, session token (encrypted at rest).
app.logs.workspace-empty: No audit records in this workspace yet
app.logs.rotate-threshold-hint: Rotates once a workspace log file fills up, in MB (0.06–64)
app.logs.keep-generations-hint: How many generations of history to keep after rotating (1–10)
app.logs.rotate-archive: Redact and store as a zip
app.logs.rotate-drop: Do not keep; discard old files once full
app.logs.rotate-archive-warning: The zip archive has password-like fields stripped and opens directly, but it is not encrypted: anyone who can read the config directory can read it
app.logs.keep-days-hint: Cleaned by file modification time; 0 means never
app.logs.dir-unavailable: The audit directory is unavailable; nothing can be written
app.logs.verbose-hint: Records raw request bodies and all request headers (may contain secrets; the current generation is encrypted at rest)
app.logs.action-archive-now: Archive now as a redacted zip
app.logs.confirm-verbose-1: From now on every API call is recorded along with its raw request body and all request headers. They may contain the host password,
app.logs.confirm-verbose-2: the sudo password, private keys and session tokens. These entries are encrypted line by line with the same .key as the host credentials before being written,
app.logs.confirm-verbose-3: but anyone who can read the config directory can decrypt them. Turn it on only while you need it for troubleshooting.
app.logs.confirm-clear-1: This deletes all audit files and archives for {v1} (about {v2}),
app.logs.confirm-clear-2: including the records currently shown on screen. This cannot be undone and nothing can be recovered.
app.logs.cleared: Audit records and archives cleared, freeing {v1}
app.logs.detail-resize-hint: Drag to resize the details pane, double-click to reset
